fb: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
The Greek form of Manasseh. Here it is the tribe, counted among the sealed in Revelation.
King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
The Greek form of Manasseh. Matthew uses it for the king of Judah in Jesus' family line, the one who reigned longest and led the nation into idols.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return

Matthew's genealogy makes him Jacob's father and grandfather to Joseph, Mary's husband. Luke gives Joseph a different grandfather, Matthat, one of the places the two lines part, probably because they trace different lines of descent.

G3137.d: Maria or Mariam (i.e. Mirjam), the name of six Christian females
fb: Jesus' mother living at the time of the New Testament
Jesus' mother. She was engaged to Joseph when Gabriel told her she would bear the Messiah, she raised Jesus in Nazareth, and she stood at the cross when he died.
Lazarus' sister living at the time of the New Testament
She sat at Jesus' feet listening while Martha did the work. This is the Mary of Bethany, sister of Martha and Lazarus, who not long before his death anointed his feet with expensive perfume.
Woman living at the time of the New Testament
Another Mary in the Gospels, one of the women at the cross and at the empty tomb, and not to be mixed up with Jesus' mother or the Mary of Bethany.
Barnabus' relative living at the time of the New Testament
A man from the New Testament, and Acts is the only book that names him.

G3173.d: big (literally or figuratively, in a very wide application)

G3195.d: to intend, i.e. be about to be, do, or suffer something (of persons or things, especially events; in the sense of purpose, duty, necessity, probability, possibility, or hesitation)

G3107.d: supremely blest; by extension, fortunate, well off

G3196.d: a limb or part of the body

G3123.d: (adverbially) more (in a greater degree)) or rather

G3142.d: something evidential, i.e. (genitive case) evidence given or (specially), the Decalogue (in the sacred Tabernacle)

G3156.d: Matthæus (i.e. Matthitjah), an Israelite and a Christian
fb: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament

A tax collector, which made him an outcast among fellow Jews for working on Rome's behalf, until Jesus called him straight from his booth to be one of the twelve. Mark and Luke call him Levi. He threw a big dinner for Jesus with other tax collectors, and early church tradition says he wrote the Gospel that carries his name, aimed at Jewish readers.

G3162.d: a knife, i.e. dirk; figuratively, war, judicial punishment

G3120.d: soft, i.e. fine (clothing); figuratively, a catamite

G3187.d: larger (literally or figuratively, specially, in age)

G3100.d: intransitively, to become a pupil; transitively, to disciple, i.e. enrol as scholar

G3144.d: a witness (literally (judicially) or figuratively (genitive case)); by analogy, a "martyr"

G3114.d: to be long-spirited, i.e. (objectively) forbearing or (subjectively) patient

G3199.d: to be of interest to, i.e. to concern (only third person singular present indicative used impersonally, it matters)

G3170.d: to make (or declare) great, i.e. increase or (figuratively) extol

G3140.d: to be a witness, i.e. testify (literally or figuratively)

G3184.d: to drink to intoxication, i.e. get drunk

G3148.d: a whip (literally, the Roman flagellum for criminals; figuratively, a disease)

G3106.d: to beatify, i.e. pronounce (or esteem) fortunate

G3158.d: Matthat (i.e. Mattithjah), the name of two Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Luke's genealogy has two men called Mathat, and this is the one further back, near Levi.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Luke's genealogy of Joseph has two men called Mathat, one near Joseph's own generation and one much further back near Levi and Melki. Little is known of either.

G3197.d: Melchi (i.e. Malki), the name of two Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Luke's genealogy has two men of the name, and this is the one further back, near Levi.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Two ancestors in Luke's genealogy share the name. One fathered Neri around the time of the Babylonian exile; the other, Janna's son and Levi's father, stands much closer to Jesus.

G3161.d: Mattathias (i.e. Mattithjah), an Israelite and a Christian
fb: Man living at the time of Exile and Return

Two of them stand next to each other in Luke's genealogy, the son of Amos and the son of Semein, both some generations above Joseph. Neither is known otherwise. The priest who started the Maccabean revolt carried the same name, but he is a different man.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Luke's genealogy has two of them in consecutive generations, and neither is mentioned anywhere else.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A name in Luke's line through David's son Nathan, between Menan and Eliakim. Nothing else is known of him.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A name in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, from David's son Nathan, a few generations above Mattatha and Melea. The Old Testament never mentions him.
Man living at the time of United Monarchy
Nathan's son and David's grandson in Luke's genealogy, which runs Jesus' line through Nathan instead of Solomon.
Man living at the time before the Flood

Enoch's son and Noah's grandfather. Genesis gives him nine hundred sixty-nine years, longer than anyone else in the Bible. By the numbers in Genesis 5 he dies the year of the flood, though the text never connects the two. A Book of Noah fragment has him travel to find Enoch when his newborn grandson does not look human.
Man living at the time before the Flood
Luke's Greek spelling of Mahalalel, Seth's descendant before the flood, in the genealogy that runs back through Noah to Adam.
Woman living at the time of the New Testament

Lazarus and Mary's sister, at Bethany. Jesus gently told her off for fussing over the meal while Mary sat and listened. Later, grieving her brother, she said one of the boldest things anyone says in the Gospels, that Jesus was the Christ, the Son of God, just before he raised Lazarus.

G3149.d: a (properly, female) breast (as if kneaded up)

G3179.d: to transfer, i.e. carry away, depose or (figuratively) exchange, seduce

G3164.d: to war, i.e. (figuratively) to quarrel, dispute

G3105.d: through the idea of insensate craving); to rave as a "maniac"

fb: Man living at the time of the New Testament

Peter cut off his right ear the night Jesus was arrested. He was the high priest's servant, and Jesus healed the ear with a touch, the last miracle recorded before the crucifixion. Only John gives his name.
Man living at the time of the New Testament

The eleven drew lots between two men who had been with Jesus since his baptism, and the lot fell on Matthias, to take Judas Iscariot's place before Pentecost. The New Testament says nothing more about him.

G3167.d: magnificent, i.e. (neuter, plural as noun) a conspicuous favor, or (subjectively) perfection

G3191.d: to take care of, i.e. (by implication) revolve in the mind

fb: Levite living at the time of the New Testament

John Mark. He set out with Paul and Barnabas and left partway through the first journey, and that later split the two men in a sharp quarrel. Peter calls him his son, and early church tradition says he wrote the Gospel of Mark from Peter's preaching.
Man living at the time of the New Testament

A prophet and teacher in the church at Antioch, with Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene and Saul. That group laid hands on Barnabas and Saul and sent them out. Luke adds that Manaen grew up alongside Herod Antipas, the man who had John the Baptist killed.

G3152.d: empty, i.e. (literally) profitless, or (specially), an idol

G3110.d: a Macedon (Macedonian), i.e. inhabitant of Macedonia

fb: The Roman province over northern Greece. Paul crossed into it after a vision of a man pleading, "Come over into Macedonia and help us," and went on through Philippi, Thessalonica and Berea, where Christian mission in Europe is usually said to begin. He came back at least twice and praised its churches for giving out of their poverty.

G3132.d: to divine, i.e. utter spells (under pretense of foretelling

G3143.d: to be adduced as a witness, i.e. (figuratively) to obtest (in affirmation or exhortation)

G3122.d: (adverbially) most (in the greatest degree) or particularly

G3194.d: Melita, an island in the Mediterranean
fb: Malta. Paul's ship ran aground there in the storm of Acts 27, and he and the others stayed three months before sailing on to Rome. Phoenicians settled it long before, then Carthage and Rome held it, and Punic inscriptions survive from that time.

G3154.d: to render (passively, become) foolish, i.e. (morally) wicked or (specially), idolatrous

G3108.d: beatification, i.e. attribution of good fortune

G3111.d: a butcher's stall, meat market or provision-shop

G3134.d: maranatha, i.e. an exclamation of the approaching divine judgment
fb: Aramaic for our Lord, come. Paul puts it at the end of 1 Corinthians, and the early church seems to have used it as a set phrase.

G3151.d: an idle (i.e. senseless or mischievous) talker, i.e. a wrangler

fb: Priest living at the time of the Patriarchs

King of Salem and priest of God Most High. He blessed Abraham and took a tenth of the spoils, and Genesis gives him no family, no birth and no death. Hebrews builds on that silence to explain how Jesus can be a priest without coming from Levi. Josephus reads the name as "the righteous king" and takes Salem for Jerusalem.

G3133.d: to extinguish (as fire), i.e. (figuratively and passively) to pass away

G3166.d: akin to G837 (αὐξάνω) and G2744 (καυχάομαι)); to talk big, i.e. be grandiloquent (arrogant, egotistic)
